newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks soften in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks soften in directionless trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares softened further in a directionless market on Tuesday and brokers said they expected the bourse to continue easier ahead of the labour day break on Thursday.
"I think people are finding it hard to buy into the market. There's a lot of trade in the second tiers compared to last week where most trades were in the blue-chips," one broker said.
He added that uncertainty over tightening of exchange controls on one-way fungability was holding buyers back in dual-listed stocks which had been providing some of the recent impetus to the market.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE)'s key industrial index dropped 71.43 points to end Tuesday at 10,877.53, depressed largely by 50-cent losses each on publishers Zimpapers to 5,950, merchant bank National Merchnat Bank to 3,400 and Alloys to 450.

Also among the day's losers, tobacco company TSL shed 30 cents to 650, blue-chip beverages, supermarket and hotel conglomerate Delta traded 25 cents off at 1,800 and newly-listed vegetable group Interfresh lost 10 cents to 280.
A few counters bucked the trend, notably tea and coffee grower Tanganda which rose 50 cents to 650 and cement producer Porthold which gained 25 cents to 1,850.
Minings were quiet with brokers saying the latest news on gold was unlikely to help the sector out of its lethargy.

In London on Tuesday morning, bears conquered bullion pushing it to a $338.95 per ounce fixing -- its lowest level since February 12 -- as increasing prospects of future IMF gold sales dealt a fresh blow to the weakening metal.
The ZSE's mining index was unmoved at 1,022.15.
